constants.name: max_object
constants.comment: The level file's objects are numbered 1 to 30; the exit is 30

constants.name: opcode_jmp
constants.comment: The JMP opcode, which arms the MOS BREAK intercept

constants.name: level_file_end
constants.comment: The end of the level file at &2700

constants.name: game_chalice_type
constants.comment: The game's object type for the Chalice

constants.name: screen_start
constants.comment: The start of MODE 2 screen memory

constants.name: map_bytes
constants.comment: The length of the wall and object-free maps

constants.name: off_map
constants.comment: A map x or y that leaves an object out of the level

constants.name: no_link
constants.comment: A free door-key link, or no door waiting

constants.name: max_level
constants.comment: The highest level number the editor saves

constants.name: wall_block_bytes
constants.comment: The length of a wall block, 4 bytes by 12 rows

constants.name: game_exit_type
constants.comment: The game's object type for the exit

subroutines.name: plot_sprite
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite
subroutines.description:
Copy sprite sprite_number to the screen with its top-left corner at byte column plot_x, pixel row plot_y. 

The four sprite tables, indexed by sprite number, give the address of its data and its size: sprite_width bytes across (two MODE 2 pixels to a byte) by sprite_height pixel rows. The data is stored row by row and is written over the screen contents without masking, so a sprite's black pixels erase what was there, and there is no clipping. The screen is laid out like MODE 2 with 640-byte character rows from &3000, so successive bytes of a sprite row are 8 bytes apart, and each pixel row starts one byte below the last, or 640-7 bytes on when it crosses into the next character row. screen_ptr walks across each row, row_start_ptr remembers where the row began, and sprite_data_ptr walks through the data; Y stays 0. sprite_width and sprite_height are left holding the sprite's size.

subroutines.name: screen_address
subroutines.title: Calculate a screen address
subroutines.description: Set screen_ptr to the screen address of byte column plot_x on pixel row plot_y: &3000 + 640 x (plot_y DIV 8) + (plot_y MOD 8) + 8 x plot_x. plot_sprite calls it once per sprite, for the top-left byte. The multiplication by 640 is done with a table inside MOS 1.20 (mos_row_offsets, two bytes per character row, high byte first), so this only works with that MOS. The high byte of 8 x plot_x is plot_x DIV 32, taken from plot_x's top three bits with four ROLs.

subroutines.name: editor_start
subroutines.title: *EDITOR: copy the plotter page and start
subroutines.description: The program's entry point, run once by *EDITOR. Copy &2700-&28FF to &0900-&0AFF (the plotter, screen_address, the packed counts, the item types and checksums, and the sprite tables), freeing &2700-&29AF for the level file, then start at editor_init. A restart (BREAK, or another level after saving) goes to editor_init directly, as the copy has been overwritten by then.

subroutines.name: editor_init
subroutines.title: Set up and choose a level
subroutines.description: An editing session runs: editor_start copies the plotter page into place; editor_init (here) asks in MODE 7 whether to edit a level (E) or start a new one (N); for E, choose_filing_system selects disc (and a drive) or tape, ask_filename reads the name and the file is *LOADed at &2700; new_level, for N, prepares an empty level instead; start_editing draws the MODE 2 map, decrypting and unpacking a loaded level with crypt_level and unpack_level; edit_loop then runs until SHIFT+S, which walls the edges (wall_edges), packs the slots back into the level file (pack_level), chooses the wall block (choose_wall_block) and saves (save_level); after the save, A comes back here for another level and Q resets the machine. editor_init itself disables ESCAPE, arms the BREAK intercept with break_to_start and points BRKV at MOS 1.20's reset entry, so that BREAK or any error at the questions (a missing file, a filing system error) resets and comes back here; there is no error message. It clears level_encrypted, as no save has encrypted the level buffer yet. It sets the map cursor's keys to ',' '.' 'A' 'Z' and last_slot to &4F, sends *TV255 1 (applied by the MODE 7 that follows) and asks the first question, leaving the answer in new_level_flag (0 edit, 1 new) for start_editing. Reached from editor_start, from break_to_start and from save_level when another level is asked for.

subroutines.name: ask_key
subroutines.title: Print a prompt and wait for one of its keys
subroutines.description: The editor's one-keypress questions: editor_init's edit or new, choose_filing_system's disc or tape and its drive, and save_level's another level or quit. Print the text at XY up to (not including) its '*', flush the input buffer and scan the keyboard with OSBYTE &7A until an answer is held, ignoring every other key. With A=0 the answers are the two keys whose internal numbers are in scratch and scratch_hi, and A returns 0 for the first or 1 for the second, nothing being echoed. Otherwise the answers are the digits 0-3 (their internal numbers in drive_keys), and the digit is echoed and returned as a character, ready for drive_command. The flush runs with X still holding the prompt's low byte, which is non-zero for every prompt, so only the input buffer is flushed. Because the keys are read by scanning, the key pressed is left in the input buffer; ask_filename flushes it before reading a name.

on_entry.A: 0 for two keys, else a drive digit

on_exit.A: 0 or 1 for the key pressed (A=0 on entry); else the digit's character

subroutines.name: new_lines
subroutines.title: Print a new line and a blank line
subroutines.description: CR, LF, LF: ends the current line and leaves a blank one, spacing out the MODE 7 questions. Called by editor_init, ask_filename, choose_filing_system and save_level.

subroutines.name: ask_filename
subroutines.title: Ask for a filename
subroutines.description: Ask for the name of the level file, for editor_init (to load) and save_level (to save). Pause for 65536 passes of a delay loop, then flush every buffer, so the key that answered ask_key's last question (still in the input buffer) is not taken as the start of the name. Print 'Filename ' and read up to seven characters, space to '~', into filename_buffer with OSWORD 0. If only RETURN is typed, go back up onto the prompt line, print 'L' after the prompt as if it had been typed, and use the one-letter name L. ESCAPE is disabled, so OSWORD 0's ESCAPE exit is not checked.

on_exit.scratch: the name's length, without its CR (1-7)

subroutines.name: new_level
subroutines.title: Start a new, empty level
subroutines.description: Reached from editor_init when N is chosen. Fill the level's wall block (&30 bytes at &2980) with &03, then fall into start_editing, which sees new_level_flag set and starts from an empty map. Nothing reads the filler: the editor draws walls with its own sprite, and choose_wall_block always replaces the block with one from Stones before the level is saved. Nothing else of the level file is prepared here; start_editing clears its object, door and key tables, and pack_level packs the slots and maps into it when saving.

subroutines.name: start_editing
subroutines.title: Set up the editing screen and edit
subroutines.description: Turn the level at &2700 (or nothing, for a new level) into the editor's own form and draw it, ready for edit_loop. Reached from editor_init once a level file is loaded, and from new_level; new_level_flag says which. The editor keeps a level as 80 item slots (slot_x, slot_y, slot_item at &0C00), its own wall_map (&2F00) and object_free_map (&7E00), and the door-key links; the level file is only read here and written by pack_level. First, an empty editor: zero the wall map and every slot (a free slot is item 0, a wall, at (0, 0)), zero cursor_flash and link_index, select MODE 2 and disarm the BREAK intercept. The MODE 2 change clears &3000-&7FFF, so only then are unpack_level and mark_object_cell copied to &7B00 and &7D80 and the object-free map at &7E00 set to &FF (no object anywhere): set_edit_screen shows just 30 character rows, &3000-&7AFF, leaving &7B00-&7FFF as hidden workspace. Free all 20 links, note no door waiting for its key, set GCOL 3,3 (exclusive-OR, so a link line drawn twice is erased), zero the four counts and turn cursor editing off. For a loaded level: decrypt it with crypt_level, take an object of type &73 (the Chalice, which only level 25 has and the editor has no item for) off the map, unpack the tables into the slots and maps with unpack_level, show the labels and counts and plot the item in every one of the 32 x 48 cells that has one. exit_placed is then set without checking that the file's exit was on the map (unpack_level has already set trapdoor_count to 8 the same way). For both: set the level file's objects 1-29, doors and keys to &FF, so that pack_level need write only the items placed; show the labels and counts (a loaded level's for the second time); put the cursor at (11, 11), the top-left of the heroes' four start cells, with the wall as the current item, the slow cursor on and colour_10 at 1 (red, as set_edit_screen set it), and fall into edit_loop.

subroutines.name: edit_loop
subroutines.title: The editing loop
subroutines.description:
The editor proper: start_editing falls into it with the map drawn, and it loops for good, until SHIFT+S saves the level. Each pass reads the keys in this order:

- f0 toggles the slow cursor (inline here). With it on, each pass first waits three frames, so the cursor steps at most one cell every four frames (move_cursor waits for one more).
- SHIFT+S saves, but only once the exit, all eight trapdoors and a key for every door (check_door_keys) are placed: *DISC and *DRIVE 0, wall_edges, pack_level, choose_wall_block (from Stones on drive 0), MODE 7, then save_level, which never returns.
- ',' '.' 'A' 'Z' move the cursor (move_cursor). With walls chosen, the cursor sprite flashes over the wall sprite on alternate passes.
- Cursor up and cursor down step logical colour 10, the walls' colour on screen, between 1 and 7 (set_colour_10), one step a press.
- '1' and '2' step the current item down and up, 0 (wall) to &0F (key), once a pass while held; show_cursor_position prints the cursor's cell first.
- SPACE places the current item (place_item). Walls go anywhere and repeat while SPACE is held; other items are refused on the map's edge, and one goes down per press, followed by show_counts.
- TAB deletes what is under the cursor (delete_item), then show_counts. The wait that follows tests B (&9B), not TAB (&9F), so holding TAB deletes again on every pass, wherever the cursor goes, and holding B with an item chosen stalls the editor.
- CTRL shows the door-key links (draw_links) while held, and drawing them again on release rubs them out.

SPACE with walls, and SPACE refused at the edge, start the next pass at once, skipping TAB and CTRL.

subroutines.name: check_door_keys
subroutines.title: Check that every door has its key
subroutines.description: One of the edit loop's three tests before SHIFT+S may save. Count the door-key links in use and compare with door_count. A link is made only when a key is placed for a waiting door, and a door can be linked only once, so equal counts mean that no door lacks its key. A door still waiting for its key is counted in door_count but has no link, so it blocks saving.

on_exit.Z: set if every door has a key
on_exit.A: the number of links in use
on_exit.scratch: the number of links in use

subroutines.name: key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: The edit loop's key test, for its fixed keys (f0, SHIFT+S, cursor up and down, '1', '2', SPACE, TAB, B and CTRL): OSBYTE &81 with the negative INKEY number in X, which returns X = Y = &FF while the key is held. move_cursor uses the same test in cursor_key_pressed, and the wall-block chooser in chooser_key_pressed.

on_exit.Z: set if the key is pressed

subroutines.name: choose_filing_system
subroutines.title: Ask for disc or tape
subroutines.description: Ask 'Disc or tape' and select the filing system the level file is loaded from or saved to: for disc, *DISC and then *DRIVE with the digit (0-3) typed at the drive prompt; for tape, *TAPE. Called by edit_level before a level is loaded, by save_level before the filename, and by catalogue before *CAT. The edit loop selects *DISC and *DRIVE 0 itself before saving, for Stones, so the choice made here comes after it.

subroutines.name: set_edit_screen
subroutines.title: Set up the editing screen
subroutines.description: Send edit_screen_vdu's &21 bytes, once start_editing has selected MODE 2: turn the text cursor off (6845 register 10), display 30 character rows (register 6), the map's 48 rows of five pixel rows needing 240, and set logical colours 10 and 9 to red and yellow. Hiding the rows from &7B00 up leaves &7B00-&7FFF free for unpack_level, mark_object_cell and object_free_map.

subroutines.name: crypt_level
subroutines.title: Encrypt or decrypt the level file
subroutines.description: Exclusive-OR each byte of the level file, &2700-&29AF, with the low byte of its offset, which is that of its address, as the game's decrypt_level does at &6B00. Doing it twice restores the bytes. start_editing calls it to decrypt a level once loaded; save_level calls it to encrypt the level after setting the checksum, first decrypting it when an earlier save in this session left it encrypted (level_encrypted).

subroutines.name: set_colour_10
subroutines.title: Show the walls in the chosen colour
subroutines.description: VDU 19,10,n,0,0,0 with n from colour_10 (1-7). Logical colour 10 is what the wall sprite (all &CC bytes) and the cursor sprite are drawn in, so this changes the walls' colour on the screen, not in the level. The edit loop calls it after cursor up or down changes colour_10.

subroutines.name: show_labels
subroutines.title: Print the counts' labels
subroutines.description: In colour 1, at column 16 beside the map, on rows 0, 4 and 8: Objs, Mons (the trapdoors, where monsters appear) and Dors, each above its count. count_labels holds the VDU 31 moves with the text. Leaves colour 7 set for show_counts, which start_editing calls next.

subroutines.name: show_counts
subroutines.title: Print the counts
subroutines.description: Objects at (17, 2), trapdoors at (17, 6) and doors at (17, 10), each under its label, as two digits in the text colour show_labels left. Called by start_editing and after each SPACE (an item, not a wall) or TAB in the edit loop.

subroutines.name: show_cursor_position
subroutines.title: Print the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: x at (17, 20) and y at (17, 21), beside the map. The edit loop calls it every pass, after the cursor and colour keys.

subroutines.name: print_number
subroutines.title: Print a two-digit number at a text position
subroutines.description: Move the text cursor to (X, Y) with VDU 31 and print A (0-99) as two digits, a leading zero included. The tens are counted by repeated subtraction of 10. show_counts and show_cursor_position use it.

subroutines.name: wall_edges
subroutines.title: Put walls round the edge of the map
subroutines.description: Place a wall in every cell of columns 0 and 31 and rows 0 and 47, closing the map on every side. The edit loop calls it first when SHIFT+S saves, before pack_level. Each goes through place_item, which leaves a cell that already holds a wall alone and otherwise clears its object-free bit too (put_item). Items cannot be placed on the edge, so every edge cell ends up a wall, except that place_item takes the top-left cell, (0, 0), for a wall already whenever a slot is free (see item_at_cursor), so that cell's wall bit is left to save_level. It leaves cursor_x at &FF, cursor_y at 47 and the current item the wall, which no later code relies on: save_level never returns to the edit loop.

subroutines.name: save_level
subroutines.title: Save the level
subroutines.description:
The last step of SHIFT+S: the edit loop has walled the map in, packed the slots and maps into the level file at &2700 and copied in the chosen wall block, then selected MODE 7. save_level also restarts itself: break_to_save comes back here after BREAK, and a level number out of range asks again from the top.

Point the BREAK intercept at break_to_save and BRKV at the reset entry, disable ESCAPE, and ask 'Level in the Dunjunz complex' for a number of up to two digits (RETURN alone: catalogue). Only 1-24 are accepted; level 25 is in Stones. The number only chooses the checksum, from the game's level_checksums: level_number is not read again, and the filename is typed separately, so a level saved under another level's filename fails the game's checksum test when it is loaded.

Wall the top-left cell, then set the level's first byte (object entry 0's x, which the game never reads) so that the &2B0 bytes sum to the checksum modulo 256: the sum is taken with that byte 0, and the byte is checksum - sum. Both of the code's branches give that value. Encrypt the level with crypt_level, choose disc or tape, ask for the filename and *SAVE name 2700+2B0, then ask 'Another level (A) or quit (Q)'. It never returns: A restarts the editor at editor_init, and Q disarms the BREAK intercept and resets the machine.

subroutines.name: catalogue
subroutines.title: Catalogue the disc or tape
subroutines.description: Reached from save_level when RETURN is pressed with no level number, so that the user can see which level files exist before choosing one. Show CAT after the prompt, as if it had been typed as the answer, choose disc or tape, *CAT, then ask for the level number again at ask_level_number, below the catalogue, without clearing the screen.

subroutines.name: choose_wall_block
subroutines.title: Choose the level's wall block
subroutines.description: Let the user pick the picture the game draws every wall of the level with. Called from the edit loop when SHIFT+S saves, after pack_level and with drive 0 selected; save_level follows. Clear the screen, show only 25 character rows, load Stones (the 24 wall blocks) at &6E80, just below them, draw the blocks in a grid four wide and six high and frame block 0. Then loop: pause for a delay loop of about 25,000 iterations, read the keys (move_chooser: ',' '.' one block, 'A' 'Z' a row) and, when the choice moved, wait for the frame and move the frame round. SPACE copies the chosen block's &30 bytes from Stones into the level file's wall block and returns. The editing screen is not restored, as save_level selects MODE 7 next.

subroutines.name: draw_wall_blocks
subroutines.title: Draw the 24 wall blocks
subroutines.description: Plot sprites &12-&29, whose data the editor's sprite tables point at the blocks in Stones at &6E80, at their places in the grid (block_place). Called once by choose_wall_block, after load_stones.

subroutines.name: move_chooser
subroutines.title: Move the chosen wall block
subroutines.description: '.' and ',' move one block on or back, 'Z' and 'A' a row of four; a move off the grid is undone, so ',' and '.' wrap from one row's end to the next row but stop at blocks 0 and 23. Only one key is taken each call, '.' first. choose_wall_block calls it once a pause and compares the two blocks afterwards to see whether the frame must be moved.

subroutines.name: chooser_key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: The wall-block chooser's copy of key_pressed: OSBYTE &81 with the INKEY number in X, testing X before Y. Used for ',' '.' 'A' 'Z' and SPACE.

subroutines.name: block_place
subroutines.title: Find a wall block's place in the grid
subroutines.description: Block n is at column n mod 4, row n div 4: plot_x = 8 x column + &1A, plot_y = 24 x row + &14. Each block is 4 bytes by 12 rows, so the grid leaves room for the frame between them.

subroutines.name: frame_block
subroutines.title: Draw or erase the frame round the chosen block
subroutines.description: Plot sprite A (&2A the frame, &2B a blank), 6 bytes by 18 rows, one byte left of and three rows above the chosen block, so that it surrounds the 4-byte by 12-row block, then plot the block again inside it, as both sprites cover it. choose_wall_block frames block 0 at the start and, when the choice moves, erases the old frame and draws the new one.

subroutines.name: show_25_rows
subroutines.title: Show 25 rows
subroutines.description: Send VDU 23,0,6,25,0,0,0,0,0,0: 6845 register 6, the rows displayed, = 25. Row 25 starts at &6E80, where load_stones puts Stones, so the wall-block chooser does not show it. Called once by choose_wall_block, before load_stones.

subroutines.name: pack_items
subroutines.title: Pack the item slots into the level file
subroutines.description:
Turn the editor's item slots back into the level file's tables, in the game's types. pack_level calls it when SHIFT+S saves, after wall_edges.

Go through the slots from the last (&4F) to the first, so that the tables come out in the reverse of the order unpack_level read them: objects into entries 1 upwards (the exit always into entry 30), trapdoors into entries 0-7, and each door with its linked key into the next door entry. Keys and free slots are skipped. Each item's game type or door sprite comes from item_types, indexed by the editor's item number. Saving needs exactly eight trapdoors and a key for every door, so every trapdoor entry and every placed door's key is written; object and door entries beyond those placed keep the &FF (off the map) that start_editing put there. The counts are left in packed_objects, packed_trapdoors and packed_doors.

subroutines.name: pack_level
subroutines.title: Pack the level for saving
subroutines.description: Called from the edit loop when SHIFT+S saves, after wall_edges and before choose_wall_block. Pack the item slots into the object, door and trapdoor tables (pack_items), then copy the wall map and the object-free map, &C9 bytes each, into the level file. save_level then sets the checksum and encrypts.

subroutines.name: load_stones
subroutines.title: Load the wall blocks
subroutines.description: *LOAD STONES (at its own address, &6E80) with VDU output off. Called by choose_wall_block, after show_25_rows has hidden the screen from &6E80 up, with disc drive 0 already selected by the edit loop. Stones holds the 24 wall blocks (&480 bytes) and then level 25, which the editor does not use. A missing Stones is an error, and BRKV resets the machine.

subroutines.name: move_cursor
subroutines.title: Move the cursor
subroutines.description: Called at the start of every edit-loop pass, after the slow cursor's wait. Wait for the frame, rub out the cursor and put back what is under it (item_at_cursor), move with the keys in key_left, key_right, key_up and key_down (',' '.' 'A' 'Z') within the 32 by 48 map, and plot the current item there as the cursor. So the cursor shows what SPACE would place. The keys are read without waiting for release, so a held key repeats every pass. A move right skips the test for left, and a move up the test for down, so with both keys of a pair held '.' and 'A' win; the cursor can still move diagonally.

subroutines.name: plot_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: At screen byte column 2x and pixel row 5y: each map cell is two MODE 2 bytes (four pixels) by five pixel rows, so the 32 by 48 map fills the left 64 bytes and 240 rows of the screen. Used to draw the cursor, the cell under it and, at start-up, every cell of a loaded level.

subroutines.name: item_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Find what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: Search the slots for an item at the cursor; failing that, look at the wall map. A free slot is item 0 at (0, 0) (see free_slot), so whenever a slot is free the top-left cell reports a wall, whatever the wall map holds there. A door is found in its slot before its wall bit is looked at. The editor's one test of a cell's contents: move_cursor, place_item, remove_at_cursor, delete_item and start_editing's drawing all use it.

on_exit.A: the item's sprite and X its slot; 0 for a wall; &FF for nothing
on_exit.map_ptr: for no item: the cell's wall-map byte
on_exit.bit_mask: for no item: the cell's bit

subroutines.name: wall_bit
subroutines.title: Find the cursor's bit in the wall map
subroutines.description: As the game lays out its maps: the byte at (y AND &F8) x 4 + (y AND 7) + (x AND &F8), bit 7 - (x AND 7). So each room of 8 by 8 cells is 8 consecutive bytes, one per cell row, with the leftmost cell in bit 7; four rooms make a 32-byte row of rooms, and six rows of rooms the map. Used to test, set and clear walls, a door's included. mark_object_cell repeats the calculation for the object-free map.

subroutines.name: put_item
subroutines.title: Put the current item in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: place_item's last step, once the item is allowed. Clear the cell's object-free bit, for every item, walls included; nothing in the editor sets it again, so deleted items leave clear bits. A wall sets the wall map's bit; anything else takes a free slot, and a key is recorded as the key of the link being made.

on_entry.link_index: for a key, its door's link

subroutines.name: remove_at_cursor
subroutines.title: Remove what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description: delete_item's last step, once it has uncounted the item and dealt with any door-key link. Free an item's slot, or clear a wall's bit in the wall map. Freeing a door's slot leaves its wall bit set, so the cell then shows a wall. The cell's object-free bit is not set again. The cell is redrawn by move_cursor on the next pass.

subroutines.name: place_item
subroutines.title: Place the current item at the cursor
subroutines.description:
In an empty cell, place the current item within the limits: one exit, eight trapdoors, 20 doors (a door is also a wall), 29 objects, and a key only when a door is waiting for one, which links the two. With a key chosen, SPACE on an unlinked door makes it the door waiting for its key (sprite &11), in place of any door waiting before. A door sets its wall bit before its count is checked, so a 21st door is refused but leaves a wall. Called from the edit loop on SPACE and by wall_edges. Apart from a door given back its own sprite, nothing is drawn here: move_cursor redraws the cell on the next pass. Refusals are silent.

A door and its key are linked in two steps. With the key chosen, SPACE on the door makes it wait (choose_door), and the next key placed anywhere becomes its key (place_key), taking a free link. A key with no door waiting is refused.

subroutines.name: restore_waiting_door
subroutines.title: Show the waiting door as it was
subroutines.description: Put the waiting door's own sprite back in its slot and plot it, by falling into plot_slot. Used by place_key when its key is placed, and by choose_door when another door is chosen to wait instead. pending_door_item is left for the caller to clear or replace.

subroutines.name: plot_slot
subroutines.title: Plot a sprite at a slot's cell
subroutines.description: At screen byte column 2x and pixel row 5y of slot X's cell: plot_at_cursor for a cell away from the cursor: a waiting door given back its sprite, and the blank sprite over the key or door deleted with its partner.

subroutines.name: find_free_link
subroutines.title: Find a free door-key link
subroutines.description: The highest link whose door is &FF, for the key being placed for the waiting door; place_key fills in its door and put_item its key. Were none free, link_index would be &FF, but a door can wait only while fewer than 20 doors are linked, so one should always be free.

subroutines.name: free_slot
subroutines.title: Free a slot
subroutines.description: Zero its item and position. A free slot is therefore item 0 at (0, 0), as start_editing leaves every slot; item_at_cursor reads that as a wall in the top-left cell. Used by remove_at_cursor and by delete_item for the partner of a deleted door or key; nothing is drawn.

subroutines.name: delete_item
subroutines.title: Delete what is in the cursor's cell
subroutines.description:
TAB in the edit loop, which calls show_counts after it. Uncount the item and remove it (remove_at_cursor). Deleting a door frees its link and removes its key too, but leaves the door's wall bit, so a wall shows where the door was; deleting a key frees its link and removes its door and the door's wall, moving the cursor to the door and back to do so. A door waiting for its key cannot be deleted; choosing another door to wait releases it. A wall is cleared. The edit loop repeats the delete each pass while TAB is held (see edit_loop).

A key with no link, which the editor never makes, would fall out of the link search into line_x_to_graphics and return with the key still in place.

subroutines.name: line_x_to_graphics
subroutines.title: Convert line_x to graphics x
subroutines.description: line_gx = line_x x 32: a cell is two screen bytes, four MODE 2 pixels, 32 graphics units wide. (delete_item also falls into it, harmlessly, when a key has no link.)

subroutines.name: line_y_to_graphics
subroutines.title: Convert line_y to graphics y
subroutines.description: line_gy = &3FF - line_y x 20: a cell is five pixel rows, 20 graphics units, counted down from the top of the screen.

subroutines.name: plot_line_point
subroutines.title: PLOT to a cell
subroutines.description: VDU 25 with plot code X and the graphics position of (line_x, line_y), the top-left corner of that cell. draw_links calls it twice a link: PLOT 68 to move to the door, PLOT 5 to draw to the key. (The A loaded before each conversion is not used.)

subroutines.name: draw_links
subroutines.title: Draw each door-key link as a line
subroutines.description: For each link in use, move to the door's cell (PLOT 68) and draw a line to its key's (PLOT 5). The lines are exclusive-OR (GCOL 3, set at start-up), so the edit loop draws them when CTRL is pressed and again, rubbing them out, when it is released. Each line runs between the cells' top-left corners.

subroutines.name: cursor_key_pressed
subroutines.title: Test a key
subroutines.description: move_cursor's copy of key_pressed: OSBYTE &81 with the INKEY number in X, from key_left, key_right, key_up or key_down.

subroutines.name: unpack_level
subroutines.title: Unpack the loaded level into the slots
subroutines.description: Turn a loaded level file into the editor's item slots, links and maps, so that it can be drawn and edited. Called once by start_editing, after crypt_level has decrypted the file at &2700 and the Chalice has been taken off the map; it runs at &7B00, copied there by start_editing, in screen memory hidden below the 30 rows shown. Read the tables from the last entry back, putting each item in the next slot down from &4F (unpack_slot): objects 30 to 1 (the exit, 30, first, into slot &4F), skipping any whose x is &80 or more, each given its editor item by item_for_type; then doors 20 to 1, likewise skipping those off the map, each with its key in the slot just below and the pair recorded as a door-key link, from link 19 down (unpack_link); then all eight trapdoors, unchecked. At most 30 + 2 x 20 + 8 = 78 of the 80 slots are filled. Last, copy the file's wall map and object-free map into wall_map and object_free_map. Counts left for show_counts and the save checks: object_count leaves out the exit (it starts at -1), door_count counts the doors and trapdoor_count is set to 8 without looking. A key is taken from the file whether or not it is on the map. pack_level reverses the order on saving, so each load and save reverses the tables.

subroutines.name: item_for_type
subroutines.title: Find the editor's item for a level type
subroutines.description: unpack_level's lookup from the game's object type (or door sprite, &1C or &1D) to the editor's item, reading item_types the other way from pack_items. Search item_types from entry 1 for the type, keeping it in bit_mask. Nothing bounds the search: a type with no item would be matched against the bytes beyond item_types (the checksums and sprite tables), and with no match at all Y would wrap to 0 and the code would run on into &7BCE, past the copied routine, which nothing copies to after the MODE 2 clear: a zero, a BRK.

subroutines.name: mark_object_cell
subroutines.title: Mark the cursor's cell as holding an object
subroutines.description: Clear its bit in the object-free map, so that the game searches its object list when a hero steps there. The byte and bit are found as wall_bit finds them, on object_free_map at &7E00 instead of wall_map. put_item calls it first for every item placed, walls, doors, keys and trapdoors included, and nothing in the editor sets a bit again, so a deleted item leaves its cell clear and the game merely searches in vain there. The map is set to all ones by start_editing and, for a loaded level, replaced by the level's own map. It runs at &7D80, copied there by start_editing, in screen memory below the 30 rows shown (&3000-&7AFF).

banners.name: break_to_start
banners.title: BREAK intercept: start again
banners.description: The MOS calls the BREAK intercept twice during a reset, first with C clear and then, once the reset is done, with C set. editor_init points the intercept here, so BREAK (or an error, since BRKV is the reset entry) while the questions are being asked returns, on the second call, to editor_init, with the editor still in memory. start_editing disarms the intercept, so BREAK while editing is an ordinary reset; save_level arms its own, break_to_save.
